facts.text: The MgAlTiVFeCo powder was consolidated by spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C.
Oxidation testing was conducted at 900 °C in air.
Corrosion testing was conducted in a 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
Sintering at 1000 °C produced a dense microstructure containing uniformly distributed oxide barrier phases, including AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3.
The high-temperature SPS treatment promoted a dense, continuous passive film that impeded chloride-ion penetration.
Oxidation exhibited biphasic parabolic kinetics, indicating diffusion-controlled oxide-scale growth.
The sample sintered at 1000 °C had better oxidation resistance than samples sintered at 850–950 °C.
The sample sintered at 1000 °C had the lowest corrosion rate and best corrosion resistance among the tested sintering temperatures.
The 1000 °C SPS sample reached a relative density of 96.7%.
The 1000 °C SPS sample reached a microhardness of 1235.5 HV.
The 1000 °C SPS sample had a corrosion current density of 1.07×10^-6 A·cm^-2.
